claim.why_it_matters: The blank page 708 carries a level-1 heading that the PDF prints only on page 709, where the markdown repeats it as '## <u>SECTION XVII: APPENDICES</u>'; the section heading is duplicated and anchored on the wrong page.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 708 is indeed blank apart from specks and the licence stamp, and page 709 prints SECTION XVII: APPENDICES, which the markdown transcribes there as '## <u>SECTION XVII: APPENDICES</u>'. But the '# SECTION XVII: APPENDICES' line on page 708 is the transcription's uniform document-outline scaffolding, not transcribed page content: every section of specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md gets a level-1 '# SECTION <n>: <title>' divider placed at the end of the preceding page, before the section's first page's '## Page N' marker (e.g. SECTION II after blank page 84, VII after blank 374, IX after blank 470, X after blank 514, XI after blank 552, XII after blank 574, and after folio lines III-26, IV-46, V-40 for non-blank predecessors). Here it follows the same convention. It attributes no text to page 708 that the standard lacks, drops nothing, and changes no meaning; it is navigation structure (formatting/scaffolding), which the review rules exclude.
